ev.q: From 2003 to 2014, a total of 1,531 suicides among AI/AN and 103,986 among whites were collected in NVDRS
AI/AN decedents had lower odds than did white decedents of having received a mental health diagnosis or mental health treatment
More than one third (35.7%) of AI/AN suicides occurred among youths aged 10–24 years
More than two thirds (69.4%) of AI/AN decedents resided in nonmetropolitan areas
AI/AN decedents were significantly more likely to test positive for marijuana
AI/AN had significantly higher odds of experiencing this circumstance (aOR = 1.2; 95% CI = 1.1–1.3)
This report includes all available 2003–2014 NVDRS data from the 18 participating states.
CDC’s NVDRS is an active state-based surveillance system that monitors the occurrence and characteristics of violent deaths, including suicides.

methods_quotes.q: Group differences were assessed using chi-squared tests and logistic regression.
Significant chi-squared results (p<0.05) were further examined using logistic regression, controlling for age and sex.
Rural-Urban Commuting Area codes were used to classify geographic areas into metropolitan and nonmetropolitan categories.
Victim residential ZIP codes were dichotomized as “metro” (RUCA codes 1–3) and “nonmetro” (RUCA codes 4–10).
Each adjusted odds ratio used white as the reference group and controlled for age group and sex.
